--- title: "Nets and dn0" --- A net enters both models as two numbers, `dn0_use`, the probability that a mosquito is killed when it contacts a treated net, and `itn_use`, the share of the population sleeping under one. Which insecticide the net carries, and how resistant the local mosquitoes have become, is compressed entirely into `dn0_use`. `calculate_dn0` does that compression. It is the first call in almost every `estimint` workflow. ## Net types Four formulations are modelled. `net_types` returns their canonical names alphabetically, which puts `ppf` before `pyrrole`. ::: {#6530fde9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from estimint import net_types, calculate_dn0 net_types() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['pyrethroid_only', 'pyrethroid_pbo', 'pyrethroid_ppf', 'pyrethroid_pyrrole'] ``` ::: ::: Each formulation has a short alias, accepted anywhere a net type is, and the aliases double as the keyword-argument names in the wider API. | Alias | Canonical name | Formulation | |---|---|---| | `py_only` | `pyrethroid_only` | Pyrethroid alone | | `py_pbo` | `pyrethroid_pbo` | Pyrethroid with PBO | | `py_ppf` | `pyrethroid_ppf` | Pyrethroid with pyriproxyfen | | `py_pyrrole` | `pyrethroid_pyrrole` | Pyrethroid with chlorfenapyr | Both spellings are case-insensitive. The canonical names are joined with `_` throughout, so a hyphen raises `ValueError: unknown net type`. ## From a net mix to dn0 `calculate_dn0` takes a resistance level and the net mix as keyword arguments, one keyword per net type, one value per share of the population using it. ::: {#932e7a16 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} net = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.70) net ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` DN0Result(dn0=0.3110000000000001, itn_use=0.7) ``` ::: ::: What comes back is a `DN0Result`, a named tuple of exactly two fields, which unpacks by position and reaches the same two values by attribute. ::: {#0e6add63 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} net.dn0, net.itn_use ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (0.3110000000000001, 0.7) ``` ::: ::: At 30% pyrethroid resistance a pyrethroid-only net kills about 31% of the mosquitoes that contact it. Coverage is 70%. Passing more than one keyword gives a mix, so that here 40% of the population has pyrethroid-only nets, 30% has PBO nets, and the remaining 30% has no net at all. ::: {#f93ef5c5 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} mix = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.40, py_pbo=0.30) mix ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` DN0Result(dn0=0.38555000000000006, itn_use=0.7) ``` ::: ::: ## dn0 and itn_use The two fields are built differently, one as an average and one as a total. `dn0` is the **usage-weighted average** of the per-net-type `dn0` values across the mix, and the weights are normalised over the nets in the mix rather than over the population. That makes it a property of the nets that exist rather than of how many people own them, so a mix covering 70% of the population has the same `dn0` as one covering 20% in the same proportions. Reconstruct it by hand. ::: {#3c24b1bd .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} only = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=1.0).dn0 pbo = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_pbo=1.0).dn0 by_hand = (0.40 * only + 0.30 * pbo) / (0.40 + 0.30) round(by_hand, 5), round(mix.dn0, 5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` (0.38555, 0.38555) ``` ::: ::: `itn_use` is the **sum** of the shares, 0.40 + 0.30 = 0.70, and it is the total ITN coverage of the population. It is already complete. ::: {.callout-warning} ## A note on `itn_use` `DN0Result.itn_use` is the finished coverage figure, not a weight awaiting a coverage term. Multiplying it by a usage fraction a second time understates the coverage. The error is silent. ::: {#dab55fb7 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} net = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.70) net.itn_use, round(net.itn_use * 0.70, 3) # the second value is the mistake ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` (0.7, 0.49) ``` ::: ::: The model then reads a district with 49% net coverage rather than 70%, and understates the EIR the setting is judged to need. The size of that error is measured in [Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd). ::: ## Resistance and dn0 Holding usage at 1.0 for one formulation at a time isolates its resistance response. ::: {#e3fdd6a3 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd levels = [0.0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0] table = pd.DataFrame( { f"{r:.2f}": [calculate_dn0(r, **{nt: 1.0}).dn0 for nt in net_types()] for r in levels }, index=net_types(), ).round(4) table.index.name = "net type" table ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
0.00 0.25 0.50 0.75 1.00
net type
pyrethroid_only 0.3376 0.3163 0.2850 0.2344 0.0000
pyrethroid_pbo 0.5094 0.4893 0.4567 0.3916 0.0714
pyrethroid_ppf 0.4111 0.3980 0.3777 0.3394 0.1085
pyrethroid_pyrrole 0.5611 0.5526 0.5371 0.4964 0.1522
``` ::: ::: Read across a row for the decay of one formulation, and down a column to compare formulations at a fixed resistance. A pyrethroid-only net falls to zero at full resistance. The other three retain some lethality across the whole range. Pyrrole nets are the most lethal and the flattest, losing about a tenth of their `dn0` between resistance 0.0 and 0.75, where a pyrethroid-only net loses nearly a third. PPF nets sit low throughout the table. Their effect on the next generation is not represented in `dn0` at all, and reaches the emulator through the `lsm` term instead. The curves come from the same source `malariasimulation` uses. ## Caveats `dn0` summarises the kill on contact and nothing else. It captures neither repellence nor the loss of a net to wear and disuse over a campaign, and one net mix is assumed to hold across the whole population. The resistance level supplied should be the local pyrethroid resistance at the decision point, and because the curves steepen above 0.75, vary it in a sensitivity check. ## See also The two numbers `calculate_dn0` returns feed the inversion set out in [Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd), which also measures how far a double-counted `itn_use` drags the inferred EIR down. Please see [Interventions and nets](../03-concepts/interventions.qmd) for the epidemiology behind the four formulations.
